subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals - ZenHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Mills <ava@zenhealth.com>, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals - ZenHealth

Hi Ava / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today - appreciate the context on your roadmap. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Lack of prompt-level observability: hard to quickly surface regressions tied to prompt or model changes.
- No canonical "golden prompt" sets to run automated evals; current checks are ad-hoc.
- Limited tracing hooks to correlate model outputs with upstream request metadata (user cohort, feature flags).
- Alerting for quality regressions is noisy / manual.

Current stack you described:
- Frontend -> internal API -> calls to OpenAI (primary LLM)
- Datadog for infra/latency metrics; Mixpanel for product events; no unified LLM observability yet
- In-house eval scripts (Python) run weekly, results in S3

Success criteria you want to hit (as discussed):
1) Detect and alert on prompt- or model-induced regressions within 24 hours of release
2) Push-button rollout guardrails so we can canary and auto-fallback model variants
3) Centralized dashboards for per-prompt quality, latency, and token-cost trends
4) Ingest and run "golden prompt" sets with regression alerting and simple A/B evaluation

What Redwood can demo / provide:
- Console dashboards: per-model, per-route, per-prompt metrics (quality+cost+latency)
- Tracing hooks to attach user/cohort metadata and feature flags to each LLM call
- Evals pipeline: ingest golden prompt sets, scheduled regressions, and regression alert policies
- Rollout guardrails: canary distributions, automatic fallback to prior model variant on quality regressions

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) We'll share a short Mutual Action Plan and a sample ingestion template for your golden prompts (attached).
2) Rishi will run a 30-45m demo of Console + Optimize focused on dashboards, evals ingestion, and rollback flow - propose Wed Jul 13 or Thu Jul 14.
3) Please send: (a) a sample of your golden prompt set (CSV preferred), (b) a short list of 3-5 high-priority routes/prompt variants, and (c) a small test dataset or S3 path we can use for a demo run.

Attachments: zenhealth-discovery-answers.pdf, sample-golden-prompts.csv

If that looks right, I'll lock the demo time and share the MAP + Drive folder.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
https://calendly.com/marissa-redwood/30min

---
Note: for demo we'll avoid any live production writes; read-only access to a staging S3 bucket is sufficient for initial evals.

From: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@zenhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Mills <ava@zenhealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Observability & evals - ZenHealth

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Top priorities: (1) regression alerts for quality, (2) rollout guardrails (auto-fallback), (3) per-prompt dashboards.
- We currently log request/response payloads into an internal S3 bucket (redacted), and Datadog picks up latency metrics. We do not send user PII to any external vendor.

Two quick asks for the demo: 
1) Can Redwood integrate traces into Datadog (we'd like to see both infra and prompt-level together)?
2) Can you show how eval results map back to specific deployments/model versions?

Also attaching a simple architecture sketch (internal) - would prefer that not be shared beyond Redwood for now.

Thanks - Tom

Thanks Tom - quick replies to your asks and what we'll cover in the demo: 

On Datadog integration:
- We surface traces and can forward correlated metadata (trace ids, request ids, user cohort tags) to Datadog so you can correlate infra and prompt quality. We'll show an example during the demo.

On mapping evals to deployments:
- Redwood Optimize stores eval results tied to model version and route. In the Console we can filter by deployment tag so you can see regressions tied to a rollout window.

Demo agenda (30-45m) - what we'll show:
- Live walk-through: per-prompt quality dashboards, token-cost trends, and alerting rules
- Evals ingestion: how to upload golden prompts, schedule runs, and configure regression thresholds
- Tracing hooks: demo of attaching user/cohort metadata and how to surface it in traces
- Rollout guardrails: canary creation, automatic performance checks, and auto-fallback demo

Prep requests (please):
- Sample golden prompt CSV (columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output or check),
- 3 priority prompt variants/routes,
- Read-only access to a small sample from your S3 (or we can accept a Drive upload).

I've attached a short demo brief to set expectations: redwood-dashboards-demo-brief.pdf

Proposed demo times (Pacific): Wed Jul 13 10:00am or Thu Jul 14 2:00pm - which works for you?

-Rishi
